title: Upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension for proper algebraic spaces
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For $t\in T$ put $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, using the residue field and its canonical point map [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Define $n_f(t)$ as the supremum of the topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of all affine schemes with a representable etale map to $X_t$; the empty fibre has dimension $-\infty$. Assume $f$ is proper: it is separated, of finite type and universally closed. Separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test; finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; universally closed means closed on underlying point spaces after every algebraic-space base change. Point spaces carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]; these are the algebraic-space versions of the scheme conventions [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Then $n_f(t)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots\}$ for every $t$, and for each integer $a\geq-1$ the set $\{t\in T:n_f(t)\leq a\}$ is open, equivalently $\{t:n_f(t)>a\}$ is closed. No flatness, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D4Q (lemma-dimension-fibres-proper), restricted to a scheme target; fibre dimension is computed on affine etale charts.

proof.text: Properness includes finite type, so apply [lem-sfb-space-fibre-dimension-supremum] to $f$. With $\delta_f(x)$ defined there by chartwise local fibre dimension, it gives $n_f(t)=\sup_{f(x)=t}\delta_f(x)$, finite when the fibre is nonempty and $-\infty$ otherwise. This is exactly the defining supremum over affine etale charts, not the dimension of the local ring at a point. Thus all asserted values of $n_f$ lie in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots\}$.

Fix an integer $a\geq0$. Finite type includes locally finite type, so [lem-sfb-space-local-fibre-dimension-open] gives an open subset $W_a=\{x:\delta_f(x)\leq a\}$ of $|X|$, with exactly the same chartwise definition of $\delta_f$ as in step 1. Its complement $Z_a=\{x:\delta_f(x)>a\}$ is closed. No finite-presentation or flatness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 0D4Q (lemma-dimension-fibres-proper), first sentence of proof, using Tag 04NT

proof.text: For $a\geq0$, the supremum formula in step 1 gives $n_f(t)>a$ if and only if some $x$ over $t$ has $\delta_f(x)>a$: if no such $x$ exists, $a$ is an upper bound, and conversely any such value is a lower bound for the supremum. Therefore $\{t:n_f(t)>a\}=|f|(Z_a)$. By the universally closed part of the assumed properness, applied to the identity base change, this image of the closed subset $Z_a$ is closed. Its complement $\{t:n_f(t)\leq a\}$ is open. This uses the explicit definition of properness in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0D4Q (lemma-dimension-fibres-proper), last two sentences of proof

proof.text: For $a=-1$, take $Z_{-1}=|X|$, a closed subset of itself. By the fibre-emptiness assertion of [lem-sfb-space-fibre-dimension-supremum] and the values already proved, $\{t:n_f(t)>-1\}=|f|(|X|)$. This is closed by the same universally closed hypothesis. Its open complement consists precisely of the empty fibres, with dimension $-\infty$. This proves the remaining threshold and completes the assertion.

lean.statement: theorem proper_fibreDimension_finite_isOpen {S : Scheme.{u}} (T : Over S) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (hf : MapIsProper f) : (∀ t : T.left, fibreDimensionOverScheme f t = ⊥ ∨ ∃ n : ℕ, fibreDimensionOverScheme f t = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ (∀ a : ℤ, -1 ≤ a → IsOpen {t : T.left | fibreDimensionOverScheme f t ≤ (if a < 0 then ⊥ else (a.toNat : WithBot ℕ∞))} ∧ IsClosed {t : T.left | (if a < 0 then ⊥ else (a.toNat : WithBot ℕ∞)) < fibreDimensionOverScheme f t})
lean.note: Reuses the published properness, scheme-as-space, and chartwise dimension definitions. fibreDimensionOverScheme is the existing etaleDimension of the actual residue-field presheaf pullback. Affine refinement identifies this with the stated supremum of affine etale chart dimensions. Integer threshold -1 is dimension bottom; nonnegative integer thresholds use their natural-number coercions.
